title: Traders Making $100M Deals on Mobile Apps - Investopedia (blog)
text:
Traders Making $100M Deals on Mobile Apps By Donna Fuscaldo January 29, 2018 — 2:05 PM EST 
Smartphones aren't only for online shopping or social media posting – all sorts of investors are increasingly using their mobile devices to conduct trades. That bodes well for the likes of Robinhood , TD Ameritrade , E*TRADE and TradeStation , the online brokerage s that have been embracing mobile in a bigger way. According to a new survey by JPMorgan , out of 400 respondents, 61% of institutional traders said that they are either somewhat or extremely likely to conduct trading and investing via a mobile app this year. That is up from just 31% of survey respondents in last year's survey. 
What's more, Bloomberg recently reported that traders are beginning to conduct deals worth more than $100 million during a single mobile transaction thanks to an increase in security on mobile devices. Smartphone makers have increasingly added biometrics to their devices, making them much more secure and giving consumers a little more confidence that their data are safe, whether they are checking their bank account or making a stock trade. In an interview with Bloomberg last week, Scott Wacker, global head of e-commerce sales and marketing at JPMorgan, said that the largest trade on its FX trading app was for more than $400 million and that $100 million trades via the app are not uncommon. 
[Check out Investopedia's Ally Invest review to learn more about this low-cost broker with powerful charting tools.] 
Of the respondents in the JPMorgan survey, 50% said that company policies preclude them from mobile trading, while 34% said that there are policies on the books at their firms that prevent them from using their mobile devices altogether. On the flip side, more than half of the institutional traders polled, or 53%, that use mobile for trading said the most important feature is the ability to sync mobile orders with the desktop, while 50% cited market data. The majority of the survey respondents in the JPMorgan poll were FX traders. 
The new survey is sure to be welcome news for some of the online brokerages that have been embracing mobile as they aim to reach new customers, particularly younger ones that are very comfortable with mobile trading. Take Robinhood as one example. In November, the mobile brokerage app geared toward millennials was closing in on E*TRADE Financial Corporation ( ETFC ) in terms of the number of accounts. And that is in just under two years. Robinhood said that it crossed the 3 million user mark and has more than $100 billion in transaction volume in the beginning of November. At the end of 2016, E*TRADE had roughly 3.6 million brokerage accounts, and it has been around for way longer than its fintech competitor. 
Meanwhile, TD Ameritrade Holding Corporation ( AMTD ), which has a mobile trading app, is seeing strong demand from that venue, with the company saying in December that it saw an uptick in mobile trades on Black Friday, with mobile increasing to 28% of trades from 24% of trades on that day in 2016. In 2015, 21% of trades during the kickoff to the holiday shopping season occurred on mobile devices. For its part, E*TRADE started letting clients trade options on mobile devices and log into their investment accounts with Apple Inc.'s ( AAPL ) Face ID in November. According to E*TRADE, futures trading should not be limited to desktop computers. 
TradeStation, which has long offered mobile trading, made enhancements in December to enable faster trading. With the upgrade, customers will be able to send and manage orders through its updated Matrix tool and save time by creating customized order defaults for each trade they make. There is also quicker order entry thanks to the ability to bypass the order confirmation dialog as well as support for Apple's iPhone X. Related Articles
